papers.title: Cultivating the Imagination of China and the Western World: Foreign Influencers on Chinese Digital Platforms
papers.authors: Zheng Li, Jie Su, and Xin Su
papers.category: 甲亢哥访华 · direct foreign-influencer evidence
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: The study examines how foreign social-media influencers on Chinese platforms mediate intercultural understanding through political, cultural, and commercial filters. This is direct foreign-influencer evidence, although it studies Chinese audiences rather than overseas followers of a China visit.

papers.title: Is an exciting outsider or a trustworthy local more persuasive? A self-construal contingent, dual-pathway model of cross-cultural travel vlogs
papers.venue: Journal of China Tourism Research, OnlineFirst
papers.category: 甲亢哥访华 · adjacent China-travel mechanism
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: Using the context of inbound travel to China, the study compares foreign outsider and local insider vlog perspectives and tests how linguistic arousal and audience self-construal shape persuasion. It separates an excitement pathway from a trust pathway to travel intention, demonstrating that a foreign creator is not uniformly more persuasive than a local one. This is a close mechanism study for IShowSpeed-style China travel content rather than a study of IShowSpeed himself.

papers.title: Language Justice and Machine Translation on Social Media
papers.category: X automatic translation · direct platform mechanism
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: This article analyzes the language-justice consequences of machine-translation systems embedded in social media. It explains how automatic translation can widen cross-language access while also exposing code-switched or community-bounded speech to unintended audiences, distorting identity-sensitive language, and creating moderation or reputational harms. The evidence is directly about platform translation, including Twitter examples, but it is a critical analysis rather than a causal test of replies or sharing.

papers.title: Generative AI and employee well-being: Exploring the emotional, social, and cognitive impacts of adoption
papers.category: Workplace AI and well-being · direct evidence
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: Survey data from about 130 knowledge workers are analyzed with partial least squares structural equation modeling to test how attitudes toward generative AI predict adoption intensity and emotional, social, and cognitive well-being. Positive attitudes increase adoption, and the extent of adoption is associated with all three well-being dimensions, with team cohesion operating as an important pathway. The cross-sectional design limits causal inference.

papers.title: Would you rather work with ChatGPT or a human coworker? Exploring the impact of generative AI on job satisfaction
papers.category: Workplace AI and well-being · direct evidence
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: A two-stage vignette experiment places participants in a time-pressured corporate communication task and compares task support from ChatGPT with support from a human coworker. ChatGPT support produces lower job satisfaction through reduced perceived organizational support and opportunity to perform and increased job insecurity. The comparison identifies social, motivational, and work-context pathways through which generative AI can reduce workplace well-being.

papers.title: Cultural Attraction and Cultural Discount: Mechanisms Influencing Chinese Film Export Box Office
papers.authors: Liu Xiaojuan, Shao Yang, and Wu Zeyu
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: Panel data from 37 countries for 2016–2024 are used to model a nonlinear relationship between cultural distance and overseas box-office performance of Chinese films. The paper distinguishes a novelty-driven cultural-attraction path from a value-resonance identification path and tests power distance and cultural clusters as boundary conditions. It is closely aligned with the dissertation’s value-fit and cultural-boundary questions, but it has not completed journal peer review.

papers.title: Beyond Performance: Replacing a Human Coworker with AI Enhances Motivation
papers.authors: Brice Corgnet, Elena Fumagalli, and Sarah Rezaei
papers.category: Preprint · workplace AI and well-being · not peer reviewed
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: In a preregistered experiment with 1,091 participants, people completed a creative task either with another human or with generative AI under matched conditions. Collaborating with AI increased perceived relatedness, competence, autonomy, job satisfaction, and interest, with reported standardized differences of roughly 0.2–0.5. The findings provide a positive counterpoint to workplace-AI strain accounts but have not completed journal peer review.

toc.title: Softening the spring: Sensitization of transient media effects through repeated exposure over time
toc.abstractEn: Repeated-exposure data are used to test whether initially transient media effects become stronger as audiences encounter similar messages over time. The study develops a sensitization account and estimates how the timing and accumulation of exposure alter effect persistence rather than assuming a constant one-shot response.

toc.title: The integrative theory of supportive network (re)structuring: a case study in the context of LGBTQ+ hate speech
toc.abstractEn: The article develops and applies an integrative theory of how people reorganize supportive communication networks after exposure to LGBTQ+ hate speech. It links harmful communication, support seeking, network activation, and relationship change to explain how social resources are mobilized and restructured.

toc.title: When it’s your own child: effects of media narratives on U.S. parents’ support for their LGBTQ+ teen
toc.abstractEn: An experiment tests how media narratives influence U.S. parents’ responses to the prospect of having an LGBTQ+ teenager. The design examines whether perspective-taking and identification with a parent-centered narrative increase supportive attitudes and intended behavior.

toc.title: Positioning enjoyment and appreciation as key components of news use
toc.abstractEn: The study argues that news use should be understood partly through the distinct experiences of enjoyment and appreciation. Survey and measurement evidence separates pleasurable engagement from meaningful or reflective responses and relates both to patterns of news consumption.

toc.title: Academic freedom: defending a public good
toc.abstractEn: This oration frames academic freedom as a public good that supports knowledge production and democratic communication. It identifies institutional and political pressures on scholarly inquiry and argues for collective rather than purely individual defenses.

toc.title: Inoculating against fatalistic beliefs: a comparative test of narrative and non-narrative strategies
toc.abstractEn: A comparative experiment tests narrative and non-narrative inoculation messages designed to reduce fatalistic beliefs. The study evaluates whether story form changes resistance, perceived threat, counterarguing, and later belief outcomes.

toc.title: Rejection of cross-cutting news depends on content, sources, and cultural contexts: evidence from online trace data
toc.abstractEn: Online trace data across cultural settings are used to examine when audiences reject politically cross-cutting news. The results show that avoidance cannot be reduced to ideological disagreement alone because content, source cues, and national context jointly shape exposure and rejection.

toc.title: Loneliness and the local news environment
toc.abstractEn: The article connects individual loneliness with characteristics of local news environments. It tests whether access to and engagement with community information correspond to social connectedness while accounting for individual and contextual differences.

toc.title: Looking good, fitting in: co-trajectories of appearance- and friendship-related identity distress and positive online self-presentation in adolescence
toc.abstractEn: Longitudinal data trace how appearance-related and friendship-related identity distress develop alongside positive online self-presentation during adolescence. The study identifies linked trajectories and clarifies which patterns of self-presentation coincide with greater or lower identity strain.

toc.title: Do good chat groups make good neighbors? Continuity and change of norms in neighbor relations under digital co-presence
toc.abstractEn: The study examines neighborhood chat groups as spaces of digital co-presence. It shows how existing norms of neighborliness persist, shift, or become contested when coordination, support, surveillance, and conflict are moved into persistent group communication.

papers.title: Emergence of polarization in networks of large language model agents
papers.evidence: Publisher or authoritative index record verified
papers.takeaway: Experiments with interacting large-language-model agents show that decentralized agents can spontaneously form social networks with homophilic clustering and polarized opinion structure. The study analyzes how local interaction and network formation amplify separation even without an externally imposed polarized topology. Its social-science relevance lies in the controlled modeling of communication, homophily, contagion, and polarization, while the agents are simulations rather than human participants.

papers.title: The influence of transportation, social norms, cultural identity, and affective disposition in transnational media enjoyment
